content: I think Analysys I is great way to mix presenting actual proof, with giving the actual excercises. Maybe if excercises can be interactive it would be helpful, since you can solve whole set of tasks online, without installing/cloning anything. Is there way to do that in Verso right now?

There is not, at the moment. For Verso, we've prioritized producing documentation that can be hosted anywhere, with commodity and free web hosting; a feature like this would require a non-trivial server setup. It would be great, but it's not the use case we've focused on yet.

For small, self-contained, single-file cases like the examples in the Lean reference manual, we can generate links to live.lean-lang.org that pre-fill the editor with the self-contained example. But that approach doesn't scale to larger examples or exercises.
What do you think proper way to have this feature if the think hypothetically, and without any commitment from the core team? Maybe it's possible to host Lean using WASM build of sort for example?

I think it would require a careful design process that we don't have the time to go through right now. I don't even have a thorough understanding of all the use cases, so the first step would be to catalogue them and figure out which ones to support. WASM Lean is one way to do it, which faces significant engineering challenges to make it small enough to make sense. A hosted server is another, which imposes constraints on users wanting to host the document.
Btw, this is also discussed in #verso > Display the contents of the infoview in Verso web pages .
